tie_reference: TIE (2026). Physics for Secondary Schools Student's Book Form 1. Dar es Salaam: Tanzania Institute of Education.
source_note: Verified Physics Form One lesson plans (Arusha Catholic Seminary). 26 lesson plans (80 min double periods, 2 per week) covering Introduction to Physics (Weeks 1-2), Measurement (Weeks 3-5), Introduction to Force (Weeks 6-8), Density and Relative Density (Weeks 9, 11), and Sinking and Floating (Weeks 12-14) for Term I. Week 10 is mid-term assessment.

lessons.title: PHYSICS FORM ONE LESSON PLAN NO. 1A (TERM I - WEEK 1, DOUBLE PERIOD - 80 min): CONCEPT OF PHYSICS
lessons.main_competence: 1.0 Demonstrate mastery of the nature of Physics, measurement, and force
lessons.specific_competence: 1.1 Explain the concept and scope of Physics
lessons.specific_activity: Explain the concept of Physics and its branches
lessons.references: TIE (2026). Physics for Secondary Schools Student's Book Form 1. Dar es Salaam: Tanzania Institute of Education.

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Asks students to name everyday objects that work using physics principles (mobile phone, bicycle, torch).
teaching_structure.learning_activities: Name everyday objects and share ideas.

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Defines Physics as the branch of science that studies matter, energy, and their interactions. Explains branches: mechanics, heat, light, sound, electricity, magnetism, and modern physics, linking each to daily life.
teaching_structure.learning_activities: Take detailed notes on the definition and branches of Physics.
teaching_structure.assessment_criteria: Correct understanding of Physics and its branches

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Students work in groups to sort given phenomena (rainbow, moving car, boiling water, magnet picking pins) under the correct branch of Physics.
teaching_structure.learning_activities: Sort phenomena under the correct branches.

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Reviews group answers, summarises the scope of Physics, and asks oral questions.

lessons.title: PHYSICS FORM ONE LESSON PLAN NO. 1B (TERM I - WEEK 1, DOUBLE PERIOD - 80 min): CONCEPT OF PHYSICS (CONT.)
lessons.main_competence: 1.0 Demonstrate mastery of the nature of Physics, measurement, and force
lessons.specific_competence: 1.1 Explain the concept and scope of Physics
lessons.main_activity: Reinforce the concept and scope of Physics
lessons.specific_activity: Describe the scope of Physics and its branches in daily life
lessons.references: TIE (2026). Physics for Secondary Schools Student's Book Form 1. Dar es Salaam: Tanzania Institute of Education.

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Recaps the definition and branches of Physics from the double period.
Explains the relationship between Physics and other subjects (chemistry, biology, geography, mathematics) and careers that require Physics (engineering, medicine, teaching, meteorology).
teaching_structure.learning_activities: Take detailed notes linking Physics to other fields.
teaching_structure.assessment_criteria: Correct understanding of Physics in other fields

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Guides group discussion matching each career to the branch of Physics it uses most.
teaching_structure.learning_activities: Match careers to branches in groups.

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Administers oral questions on the scope of Physics and its branches.

lessons.title: PHYSICS FORM ONE LESSON PLAN NO. 2A (TERM I - WEEK 2, DOUBLE PERIOD - 80 min): CONTRIBUTION OF PHYSICS TO THE DEVELOPMENT OF MODERN SOCIETY
lessons.main_competence: 1.0 Demonstrate mastery of the nature of Physics, measurement, and force
lessons.specific_competence: 1.2 Analyze the role and theoretical basis of Physics
lessons.main_activity: Explain Physics in society and its theories
lessons.specific_activity: Discuss the contribution of Physics to modern society and outline key theories/principles of Physics
lessons.references: TIE (2026). Physics for Secondary Schools Student's Book Form 1. Dar es Salaam: Tanzania Institute of Education.

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Shows a mobile phone and asks students how electricity, waves, and materials science make it work.
teaching_structure.learning_activities: Observe the phone and share ideas.

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Explains the contribution of Physics to modern society: transport (vehicles, aircraft), communication (phones, radio, internet), medicine (X-rays, imaging), agriculture (machinery, irrigation), and energy (electricity generation).
teaching_structure.learning_activities: Take detailed notes on the applications of Physics.

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Students in groups study picture cards of technological inventions and identify the physics behind each.
teaching_structure.learning_activities: Identify the physics behind each invention.

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Reviews group findings and administers a short quiz on contributions of Physics.

lessons.title: PHYSICS FORM ONE LESSON PLAN NO. 2B (TERM I - WEEK 2, DOUBLE PERIOD - 80 min): THEORIES AND PRINCIPLES OF PHYSICS
lessons.main_competence: 1.0 Demonstrate mastery of the nature of Physics, measurement, and force
lessons.specific_competence: 1.2 Analyze the role and theoretical basis of Physics
lessons.main_activity: Reinforce the role and theoretical basis of Physics
lessons.specific_activity: Outline key theories and principles of Physics with examples
lessons.references: TIE (2026). Physics for Secondary Schools Student's Book Form 1. Dar es Salaam: Tanzania Institute of Education.

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Recaps the contributions of Physics discussed in the double period.
Outlines classic principles of Physics: Newton's laws of motion, the law of gravity, and the principle of conservation of energy, with simple examples of each.
teaching_structure.learning_activities: Take detailed notes on key theories and principles.

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Guides students to match each principle to a real-life example (ball falling, bicycle stopping, battery powering a torch).
Reviews answers, clarifies common errors, and asks oral questions.

lessons.title: PHYSICS FORM ONE LESSON PLAN NO. 3A (TERM I - WEEK 3, DOUBLE PERIOD - 80 min): CONCEPT OF MEASUREMENT
lessons.main_competence: 1.0 Demonstrate mastery of the nature of Physics, measurement, and force
lessons.specific_activity: Examine the meaning and importance of measurement in Physics
lessons.references: TIE (2026). Physics for Secondary Schools Student's Book Form 1. Dar es Salaam: Tanzania Institute of Education.

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Asks students how tall they are and how we know, prompting a discussion on measuring.
Explains the meaning of measurement (comparing a quantity with a standard unit), its importance in daily life and science, and introduces SI units as the international standard.
teaching_structure.learning_activities: Take detailed notes on measurement and SI units.

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Guides an estimation activity: students estimate the length and width of their desk, then measure with a ruler and compare.
Discusses why measurement must be accurate and consistent, then asks oral questions.

lessons.title: PHYSICS FORM ONE LESSON PLAN NO. 3B (TERM I - WEEK 3, DOUBLE PERIOD - 80 min): CONCEPT OF MEASUREMENT (CONT.)
lessons.main_competence: 1.0 Demonstrate mastery of the nature of Physics, measurement, and force
lessons.specific_activity: Apply the meaning and importance of measurement through estimation activities
lessons.references: TIE (2026). Physics for Secondary Schools Student's Book Form 1. Dar es Salaam: Tanzania Institute of Education.

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Recaps the meaning and importance of measurement from the double period.
Explains estimation, accuracy, and how to avoid common measuring errors (parallax error on a ruler, incorrect starting point).
teaching_structure.learning_activities: Take detailed notes on accuracy and errors.

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Students practise measuring different classroom objects and record the correct reading, discussing sources of error.
teaching_structure.learning_activities: Measure objects and record correct readings.

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Reviews a few readings, highlights common errors, and reinforces good technique.

lessons.title: PHYSICS FORM ONE LESSON PLAN NO. 4A (TERM I - WEEK 4, DOUBLE PERIOD - 80 min): PHYSICAL QUANTITIES AND THEIR UNITS
lessons.main_competence: 1.0 Demonstrate mastery of the nature of Physics, measurement, and force
lessons.specific_competence: 2.2 Identify physical quantities and their units
lessons.specific_activity: Distinguish fundamental and derived physical quantities and their SI units
lessons.references: TIE (2026). Physics for Secondary Schools Student's Book Form 1. Dar es Salaam: Tanzania Institute of Education.

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Asks students what is meant when a car travels at 60 km/h.
teaching_structure.learning_activities: Share ideas about speed and units.

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Defines a physical quantity as a property that can be measured. Distinguishes fundamental quantities (length, mass, time, temperature, electric current, amount of substance, luminous intensity) from derived quantities and states base SI units.
teaching_structure.learning_activities: Take detailed notes on quantities and units.
teaching_structure.assessment_criteria: Correct distinction of fundamental and derived quantities

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Students classify a list of physical quantities into fundamental or derived using a chart of SI units.
Reviews the classification and administers a matching quiz on quantities and SI units.

lessons.title: PHYSICS FORM ONE LESSON PLAN NO. 4B (TERM I - WEEK 4, DOUBLE PERIOD - 80 min): PHYSICAL QUANTITIES AND THEIR UNITS (CONT.)
lessons.main_competence: 1.0 Demonstrate mastery of the nature of Physics, measurement, and force
lessons.specific_competence: 2.2 Identify physical quantities and their units
lessons.specific_activity: Convert and apply SI units of common physical quantities
lessons.references: TIE (2026). Physics for Secondary Schools Student's Book Form 1. Dar es Salaam: Tanzania Institute of Education.

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Recaps fundamental and derived quantities from the double period.
Explains derived quantities further (area, volume, speed, density) and how their units are formed from base units; introduces unit prefixes (kilo, milli, centi).
teaching_structure.learning_activities: Take detailed notes on derived units and prefixes.

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Students convert simple measurements between units (kg to g, m to cm) and write units for given derived quantities.
teaching_structure.learning_activities: Convert units and write derived units.

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Marks sample conversions on the board and clarifies common errors.

lessons.title: PHYSICS FORM ONE LESSON PLAN NO. 5A (TERM I - WEEK 5, DOUBLE PERIOD - 80 min): BASIC EQUIPMENT/APPARATUS AND THEIR USES
lessons.main_competence: 1.0 Demonstrate mastery of the nature of Physics, measurement, and force
lessons.specific_activity: Identify basic equipment (metre rule, vernier calipers, micrometer screw gauge, stopwatch, beam balance) and their uses
lessons.teaching_learning_resources: Metre rules, vernier calipers, micrometer screw gauges, stopwatches, beam balance.
lessons.references: TIE (2026). Physics for Secondary Schools Student's Book Form 1. Dar es Salaam: Tanzania Institute of Education.

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Asks students how to measure the thickness of one sheet of paper.
teaching_structure.learning_activities: Suggest ways to measure small thickness.

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Identifies basic measuring apparatus and their uses: metre rule (length), vernier calipers and micrometer screw gauge (small lengths/thicknesses), stopwatch (time), beam balance (mass).
teaching_structure.learning_activities: Take detailed notes on each apparatus and its use.
teaching_structure.assessment_criteria: Correct identification of apparatus and uses

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Hands-on activity: students handle each apparatus, identify its parts, and measure given objects (thickness of a pencil, length of a book, time for a swing).
Administers a practical identification test on the apparatus.

lessons.title: PHYSICS FORM ONE LESSON PLAN NO. 5B (TERM I - WEEK 5, DOUBLE PERIOD - 80 min): BASIC EQUIPMENT/APPARATUS AND THEIR USES (CONT.)
lessons.main_competence: 1.0 Demonstrate mastery of the nature of Physics, measurement, and force
lessons.specific_activity: Take correct readings from measuring apparatus
lessons.teaching_learning_resources: Metre rules, vernier calipers, micrometer screw gauges, stopwatches, beam balance.
lessons.references: TIE (2026). Physics for Secondary Schools Student's Book Form 1. Dar es Salaam: Tanzania Institute of Education.

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Recaps the apparatus studied in the double period.
teaching_structure.learning_activities: Recall the apparatus and their uses.

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Explains how to read each apparatus correctly (main scale and vernier scale, thimble scale, stopwatch reading, beam balance riders) and the idea of the least count.
teaching_structure.learning_activities: Take detailed notes on correct reading.

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Students take several readings with the vernier calipers and micrometer and compare with metre rule readings.
Reviews readings and administers oral questions on reading scales.

lessons.title: PHYSICS FORM ONE LESSON PLAN NO. 6A (TERM I - WEEK 6, DOUBLE PERIOD - 80 min): CONCEPT OF FORCE
lessons.main_competence: 2.0 Demonstrate mastery of force, density, and floatation
lessons.specific_activity: Examine the meaning of force and its measurement using a spring balance
lessons.references: TIE (2026). Physics for Secondary Schools Student's Book Form 1. Dar es Salaam: Tanzania Institute of Education.

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Pushes a book on the table and kicks a ball, asking what makes them move.
teaching_structure.learning_activities: Observe and suggest what causes motion.

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Defines force as a push or a pull acting on an object, describes how force is measured using a spring balance, and introduces the SI unit newton (N).
teaching_structure.learning_activities: Take detailed notes on the definition of force and its unit.

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Students use a spring balance to pull objects of different masses and record the force needed.
teaching_structure.learning_activities: Measure forces with the spring balance.

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Reviews the readings, links force to the newton, and asks oral questions.

lessons.title: PHYSICS FORM ONE LESSON PLAN NO. 6B (TERM I - WEEK 6, DOUBLE PERIOD - 80 min): CONCEPT OF FORCE (CONT.)
lessons.main_competence: 2.0 Demonstrate mastery of force, density, and floatation
lessons.specific_activity: Measure force using a spring balance and state the SI unit of force
lessons.references: TIE (2026). Physics for Secondary Schools Student's Book Form 1. Dar es Salaam: Tanzania Institute of Education.

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Recaps how force is measured with a spring balance.
teaching_structure.learning_activities: Recall how to read the spring balance.

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Explains mass versus weight (weight is the force of gravity, W = mg), and how a spring balance measures weight as a force.
teaching_structure.learning_activities: Take detailed notes on mass and weight.
teaching_structure.assessment_criteria: Correct understanding of mass and weight

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Students measure the weight of different objects with a spring balance and record them in newtons.
Reviews the results and reinforces the difference between mass and weight.
teaching_structure.assessment_criteria: Correct distinction of mass and weight

lessons.title: PHYSICS FORM ONE LESSON PLAN NO. 7A (TERM I - WEEK 7, DOUBLE PERIOD - 80 min): EFFECTS OF FORCES
lessons.main_competence: 2.0 Demonstrate mastery of force, density, and floatation
lessons.specific_activity: Examine how force changes shape, size, speed, and direction of objects
lessons.references: TIE (2026). Physics for Secondary Schools Student's Book Form 1. Dar es Salaam: Tanzania Institute of Education.

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Stretches a spring and squeezes a ball, asking students what happens to each object.
Explains the effects of forces: changing shape and size (stretching a spring), changing speed (starting or stopping motion), changing direction (kicking a ball), often several effects at once.
teaching_structure.learning_activities: Take detailed notes on the effects of force.
teaching_structure.assessment_criteria: Correct explanation of effects of force

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Students in groups stretch springs, bounce balls, and push blocks, recording the effect observed in each case.
Reviews group observations and administers a short written test on effects of force.

lessons.title: PHYSICS FORM ONE LESSON PLAN NO. 7B (TERM I - WEEK 7, DOUBLE PERIOD - 80 min): EFFECTS OF FORCES (CONT.)
lessons.main_competence: 2.0 Demonstrate mastery of force, density, and floatation
lessons.specific_activity: Identify real-life examples of the effects of forces
lessons.references: TIE (2026). Physics for Secondary Schools Student's Book Form 1. Dar es Salaam: Tanzania Institute of Education.

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Recaps the effects of force demonstrated in the double period.
Explains real-life examples of force effects: braking a bicycle (changes speed), bending a wire (changes shape), hitting a ball (changes direction).
teaching_structure.learning_activities: Take detailed notes with real-life examples.

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Students in groups identify and record the effect of force in given picture cards and justify their choices.
Reviews the answers and clarifies any misconceptions.

lessons.title: PHYSICS FORM ONE LESSON PLAN NO. 8A (TERM I - WEEK 8, DOUBLE PERIOD - 80 min): TYPES OF FORCES
lessons.main_competence: 2.0 Demonstrate mastery of force, density, and floatation
lessons.specific_activity: Differentiate contact forces (friction, tension) and non-contact forces (gravitational, magnetic, electrostatic)
lessons.references: TIE (2026). Physics for Secondary Schools Student's Book Form 1. Dar es Salaam: Tanzania Institute of Education.

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Asks students what force is at work when a magnet holds a pin on the board without touching it.
teaching_structure.learning_activities: Share ideas about the magnet's force.

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Classifies forces as contact forces (friction, tension, applied push/pull, normal reaction) and non-contact forces (gravitational, magnetic, electrostatic), explaining how each acts.
teaching_structure.learning_activities: Take detailed notes on types of forces.

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Students sort given scenarios into contact and non-contact forces, and observe demonstrations of friction (rubbing hands) and magnetism (picking pins).
Reviews the classification and administers a classification quiz.

lessons.title: PHYSICS FORM ONE LESSON PLAN NO. 8B (TERM I - WEEK 8, DOUBLE PERIOD - 80 min): TYPES OF FORCES (CONT.)
lessons.main_competence: 2.0 Demonstrate mastery of force, density, and floatation
lessons.specific_activity: Classify forces in given scenarios and cite applications
lessons.references: TIE (2026). Physics for Secondary Schools Student's Book Form 1. Dar es Salaam: Tanzania Institute of Education.

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Recaps contact and non-contact forces using a magnet.
teaching_structure.learning_activities: Recall the two classes of force.

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Explains everyday applications: friction when walking or braking (contact), gravity holding objects down (non-contact), and uses of magnets.
Guides group activity classifying more scenarios (leaf falling, book on a table, comb attracting paper) as contact or non-contact forces.
Administers oral questions and clarifies misconceptions.

lessons.title: PHYSICS FORM ONE LESSON PLAN NO. 9A (TERM I - WEEK 9, DOUBLE PERIOD - 80 min): CONCEPT OF DENSITY
lessons.main_competence: 2.0 Demonstrate mastery of force, density, and floatation
lessons.specific_activity: Determine density of regular and irregular solids using mass and volume
lessons.teaching_learning_resources: Beam balance, measuring cylinders, solid samples.
lessons.references: TIE (2026). Physics for Secondary Schools Student's Book Form 1. Dar es Salaam: Tanzania Institute of Education.

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Asks students which is heavier: a kilogram of feathers or a kilogram of iron, then why iron feels denser.
Defines density as mass per unit volume (density = mass divided by volume) with the SI unit kg/m^3, and explains the concept of mass and volume measurement.
teaching_structure.learning_activities: Take detailed notes on the density formula.
teaching_structure.assessment_criteria: Correct understanding of the density formula

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Students measure the mass (beam balance) and volume (measuring cylinder) of regular and irregular solids, then compute density.
teaching_structure.learning_activities: Measure mass and volume and compute density.

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Reviews the computed densities and administers a calculation test.

lessons.title: PHYSICS FORM ONE LESSON PLAN NO. 9B (TERM I - WEEK 9, DOUBLE PERIOD - 80 min): CONCEPT OF DENSITY (CONT.)
lessons.main_competence: 2.0 Demonstrate mastery of force, density, and floatation
lessons.specific_activity: Calculate density of solids and liquids from measured mass and volume
lessons.references: TIE (2026). Physics for Secondary Schools Student's Book Form 1. Dar es Salaam: Tanzania Institute of Education.

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Recaps the density formula and the practical results from the double period.
Works through numerical examples of density of solids and liquids, including using the measuring cylinder to find the volume of a liquid.
teaching_structure.learning_activities: Take detailed notes and follow worked examples.

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Students solve density problems and determine the density of a liquid sample.
Marks sample answers on the board and clarifies common errors.

lessons.title: PHYSICS FORM ONE LESSON PLAN NO. 10A (TERM I - WEEK 11, DOUBLE PERIOD - 80 min): RELATIVE DENSITY OF A SUBSTANCE
lessons.main_competence: 2.0 Demonstrate mastery of force, density, and floatation
lessons.specific_activity: Calculate relative density of solids and liquids relative to water
lessons.teaching_learning_resources: Density bottles, measuring cylinders, water, calculators.
lessons.references: TIE (2026). Physics for Secondary Schools Student's Book Form 1. Dar es Salaam: Tanzania Institute of Education.

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Asks students whether oil floats on water and why, introducing comparison with water.
Defines relative density as the ratio of the density of a substance to the density of water (no units), and explains how to find it using a density bottle.
teaching_structure.learning_activities: Take detailed notes on relative density.

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Students use a density bottle to determine the relative density of a liquid by weighing it empty, filled with water, and filled with the liquid.
Reviews the results, compares with textbook values, and administers oral questions.

lessons.title: PHYSICS FORM ONE LESSON PLAN NO. 10B (TERM I - WEEK 11, DOUBLE PERIOD - 80 min): RELATIVE DENSITY OF A SUBSTANCE (CONT.)
lessons.main_competence: 2.0 Demonstrate mastery of force, density, and floatation
lessons.specific_activity: Solve problems on relative density and cite its applications
lessons.teaching_learning_resources: Density bottles, measuring cylinders, water, calculators.
lessons.references: TIE (2026). Physics for Secondary Schools Student's Book Form 1. Dar es Salaam: Tanzania Institute of Education.

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Recaps relative density and how it was measured with the density bottle.
Works through calculation problems on relative density of solids and liquids, and cites applications (checking purity of milk, battery acid testing).
teaching_structure.learning_activities: Take detailed notes and follow worked examples.

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Students solve relative density problems using mass ratios for solid and liquid samples.
Marks sample answers, clarifies errors, and discusses applications.

lessons.title: PHYSICS FORM ONE LESSON PLAN NO. 11A (TERM I - WEEK 12, DOUBLE PERIOD - 80 min): CONCEPT OF SINKING AND FLOATING
lessons.main_competence: 2.0 Demonstrate mastery of force, density, and floatation
lessons.specific_activity: Examine why objects sink or float and the concept of upthrust
lessons.teaching_learning_resources: Water tank, assorted objects of varying density.
lessons.references: TIE (2026). Physics for Secondary Schools Student's Book Form 1. Dar es Salaam: Tanzania Institute of Education.

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Drops a stone and a piece of wood into a tank of water, asking students to predict what happens.
Explains why objects sink or float by comparing their density with water's density, and introduces upthrust as the upward force exerted by a liquid on a submerged object.
teaching_structure.learning_activities: Take detailed notes on sinking, floating, and upthrust.
teaching_structure.assessment_criteria: Correct understanding of sinking and floating

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Students test assorted objects (stone, wood, coin, cork, egg) in a water tank, recording which sink and which float and why.
teaching_structure.learning_activities: Perform the sink-or-float practical and record results.

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Reviews the results and consolidates the density comparison rule, with oral questions.

lessons.title: PHYSICS FORM ONE LESSON PLAN NO. 11B (TERM I - WEEK 12, DOUBLE PERIOD - 80 min): CONCEPT OF UPTHRUST
lessons.main_competence: 2.0 Demonstrate mastery of force, density, and floatation
lessons.specific_activity: Measure upthrust on submerged objects by weighing them in air and water
lessons.teaching_learning_resources: Spring balance, overflow can, measuring cylinder.
lessons.references: TIE (2026). Physics for Secondary Schools Student's Book Form 1. Dar es Salaam: Tanzania Institute of Education.

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Asks students why a heavy ship floats while a small nail sinks.
Explains upthrust in detail: an object in a liquid feels lighter because the liquid pushes it upward, and shows how upthrust is measured by weighing an object in air and in water.
teaching_structure.learning_activities: Take detailed notes on measuring upthrust.

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Students weigh an object with a spring balance in air, then in water, recording the upthrust (loss of weight).
teaching_structure.learning_activities: Measure weight in air and water.

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Reviews the results and consolidates the meaning of upthrust with oral questions.

lessons.title: PHYSICS FORM ONE LESSON PLAN NO. 12A (TERM I - WEEK 13, DOUBLE PERIOD - 80 min): ARCHIMEDES' PRINCIPLE
lessons.main_competence: 2.0 Demonstrate mastery of force, density, and floatation
lessons.specific_activity: Verify Archimedes' Principle through practical displacement of water
lessons.teaching_learning_resources: Spring balance, overflow can, measuring cylinder.
lessons.references: TIE (2026). Physics for Secondary Schools Student's Book Form 1. Dar es Salaam: Tanzania Institute of Education.

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Asks students why it is easier to lift a bucket of water when it is still in the water.
teaching_structure.learning_activities: Share ideas about lifting in water.

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: States Archimedes' Principle: an object wholly or partly immersed in a fluid is buoyed up by a force equal to the weight of the fluid displaced, with a worked example.
teaching_structure.learning_activities: Take detailed notes on Archimedes' Principle.

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Students perform the displacement practical: weigh an object in air and in water over an overflow can, collect the displaced water, and compare its weight with the loss of weight.
Reviews the comparison and confirms Archimedes' Principle, then administers a practical test.

lessons.title: PHYSICS FORM ONE LESSON PLAN NO. 12B (TERM I - WEEK 13, DOUBLE PERIOD - 80 min): ARCHIMEDES' PRINCIPLE (CONT.)
lessons.main_competence: 2.0 Demonstrate mastery of force, density, and floatation
lessons.specific_activity: Apply Archimedes' Principle to solve problems and real-life situations
lessons.teaching_learning_resources: Spring balance, overflow can, measuring cylinder.
lessons.references: TIE (2026). Physics for Secondary Schools Student's Book Form 1. Dar es Salaam: Tanzania Institute of Education.

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Recaps Archimedes' Principle and the displacement practical.
Explains applications of Archimedes' Principle: hydrometers, submarines, ships, and hot-air balloons, and works through calculation examples of upthrust.
teaching_structure.learning_activities: Take detailed notes on applications and examples.

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Students solve calculation problems on upthrust and displaced weight.
Marks sample answers, clarifies errors, and reinforces the applications.

lessons.title: PHYSICS FORM ONE LESSON PLAN NO. 13A (TERM I - WEEK 14, DOUBLE PERIOD - 80 min): LAW OF FLOATATION
lessons.main_competence: 2.0 Demonstrate mastery of force, density, and floatation
lessons.specific_activity: Apply the Law of Floatation to explain floatation of ships/objects
lessons.references: TIE (2026). Physics for Secondary Schools Student's Book Form 1. Dar es Salaam: Tanzania Institute of Education.

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Floats a loaded model boat and asks why the boat stays afloat while a piece of the same material sinks when solid.
States the Law of Floatation: a floating body displaces its own weight of fluid, and explains why ships made of iron float because of their shape.
teaching_structure.learning_activities: Take detailed notes on the Law of Floatation.
teaching_structure.assessment_criteria: Correct statement of the Law of Floatation

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Students float model boats and observe how deep they sink with different loads, linking to displaced water.
teaching_structure.learning_activities: Float model boats and record sinking depth.

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Reviews the observations, ties the law back to Archimedes' Principle, and asks oral questions.

lessons.title: PHYSICS FORM ONE LESSON PLAN NO. 13B (TERM I - WEEK 14, DOUBLE PERIOD - 80 min): TERM I REVISION
